question: Who is the new Prime Minister of Canada?
why: As of Oct 2026, Mark Carney is Prime Minister of Canada. He became Liberal leader in March 2025 and won the April 2025 election.
rel: Justin Trudeau resigned as Liberal leader in 2025. Ottawa is Canada's capital.

question: Who was Babur’s son and successor?
why: Humayun succeeded his father Babur in 1530.
rel: Babur won the First Battle of Panipat in 1526. Humayun ruled 1530-1540 and again from 1555.

question: What was Gilgit-Baltistan’s population?
why: The 2023 census gave Gilgit-Baltistan a population of 1,709,049. The 2017 census figure was about 1.49 million.
rel: Gilgit-Baltistan is not one of Pakistan's four provinces. Its capital is Gilgit.
problem: Question has no date. Source gives 1.49 million (2017 census); latest 2023 census figure is 1.71 million, used here. Wrong options are far from both figures.

question: Where is NATO headquarters?
why: NATO headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium.
rel: NATO was founded on 4 April 1949. Its HQ is in the Haren area of Brussels.

question: Who was Pakistan’s Army Commander-in-Chief during the 1965 war?
why: Gen. Muhammad Musa Khan was Army Commander-in-Chief in the 1965 war.
rel: The war began in September 1965. Ayub Khan was President.

question: Who is known as the father of robotics?
why: Joseph Engelberger is called the father of industrial robotics because he commercialized the Unimate robot.
rel: George Devol patented an early programmable robot. Karel Capek coined the word 'robot'.

question: Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh?
why: As of Oct 2026, Syed Murad Ali Shah is Chief Minister of Sindh, in his third consecutive term.
rel: He first took office in 2016. Kamran Tessori is Governor of Sindh, not Chief Minister.

question: What symbol is used for the set of rational numbers?
why: Q is the symbol for rational numbers (quotient, p/q).
rel: R is for real numbers, Z for integers, N for natural numbers.

question: Who founded Dawn newspaper?
why: Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941.
rel: Dawn later moved to Pakistan. It is a major English-language newspaper.

question: What does CPEC stand for?
why: CPEC stands for China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.
rel: It is part of China's Belt and Road Initiative. It covers transport, energy and infrastructure.

question: What is the real cube root of unity?
why: The real cube root of 1 is 1.
rel: x^3 = 1 has roots 1 and (-1 ± i√3)/2. The two complex roots are conjugates.

question: Which country is known as the Land of the Rising Sun?
why: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun because Nippon means origin of the sun.
rel: Tokyo is Japan's capital.

question: Who is Pakistan's Federal Minister for Railways?
why: As of Oct 2026, Muhammad Hanif Abbasi is Federal Minister for Railways.
rel: Bilal Azhar Kayani is listed as State Minister for Railways. Saad Rafique and Sheikh Rashid were earlier ministers.

question: What is the smallest continent?
why: In the seven-continent model, Australia is the smallest continent.
rel: Oceania is a wider region including New Zealand and Pacific islands.

question: What was Hazrat Hamza's relationship to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
why: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was the Prophet's paternal uncle and companion.
rel: He was martyred at Uhud in 3 AH. He is called Asadullah (Lion of Allah).

question: What are Laat and Uzza?
options: Names of two mountains near Makkah
Names of two wells of Makkah
why: Al-Lat and al-Uzza were idols worshipped in pre-Islamic Arabia.
rel: They are named in Surah An-Najm (53:19-20). The third is Manat.

question: When was the Nehru Report published?
why: The Nehru Report was published on 30 August 1928 under Motilal Nehru.
rel: Jinnah answered with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

question: What is the capital of Sri Lanka?
why: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is Sri Lanka's legislative capital.
rel: Colombo is the largest city and commercial centre. Sri Lanka is an island in the Indian Ocean.
problem: Many quiz keys say Colombo, which is the commercial capital; Colombo is left out of the options because it is arguably also correct.

question: Who was the first Pakistani to travel to space?
why: Namira Salim flew on Virgin Galactic's Galactic 04 mission in October 2023 and was the first Pakistani in space.
rel: The flight was suborbital. Pakistan has no government astronaut on an orbital mission yet.

question: When was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born?
why: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah around 570 CE, in the Year of the Elephant.
rel: Some sources say 571 CE. The exact year is an estimate.
problem: Exact year is 570 or 571 CE; 570 chosen as the standard answer.

question: When was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah signed?
why: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was signed in 6 AH (628 CE).
rel: It was a truce between Madinah and the Quraysh. It came before the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

question: What role did the World Bank play in the Indus Waters Treaty?
options: It mediated and helped broker the treaty
It was a signatory in place of Pakistan
It built the Tarbela Dam alone
why: The World Bank brokered the treaty, signed by India and Pakistan in 1960.
rel: It was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960. It divides the Indus system waters.

question: In which expedition did the Muslims return without a major battle?
why: At Tabuk (9 AH) the Muslims returned without a full battle.
rel: Tabuk is in northwestern Saudi Arabia. It took place in heat and scarcity.
problem: Other expeditions also ended without fighting; Tabuk is the standard MCQ answer.

question: Who led the opposing Meccan force at the Battle of Uhud?
why: Abu Sufyan led the Meccan army at Uhud. Khalid ibn al-Walid commanded the cavalry.
rel: Uhud was in 3 AH (625 CE). Khalid later became Muslim.
problem: Khalid ibn al-Walid led the cavalry, so he is not used as an option.

question: Which vitamin supports wound healing?
why: Vitamin C is needed to make collagen, which helps wounds heal.
rel: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Its deficiency causes scurvy.
problem: Vitamin A and protein also help wound healing, but Vitamin C is the standard answer.

question: When was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's “Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind” (“The Causes of the Indian Revolt”) published?
why: Sir Syed's Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind was published in 1858.
rel: The uprising began at Meerut on 10 May 1857. Sir Syed blamed British policies.

question: Who was the last prophet sent to the Children of Israel, according to Islamic belief?
why: Isa (AS) was the last prophet sent to Bani Israel before Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
rel: Isa was born to Maryam. Muhammad (PBUH) is the final prophet.

question: What was Hudaybiyyah?
options: A place near Makkah where a treaty was signed
why: Hudaybiyyah is a place near Makkah where the 6 AH treaty was concluded.
rel: The treaty gave a truce between Muslims and Quraysh. It followed the Prophet's attempted pilgrimage.

question: For what purpose is Salat al-Istisqa offered?
why: Salat al-Istisqa is offered to ask Allah for rain during drought.
rel: It is usually prayed in congregation. Istisqa means seeking water.

question: The FSB is the security agency of which country?
why: The FSB is the Federal Security Service of Russia.
rel: It is a domestic security and counterintelligence agency.

question: Which Surah was recited before Najashi by Ja'far ibn Abi Talib?
why: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib recited Surah Maryam before Najashi.
rel: This was during the migration to Abyssinia. It speaks of Maryam and Isa.

question: A helicopter uses 50 gallons to travel 320 km. How much fuel is needed for 400 km at the same rate?
why: Fuel per km is 50/320, so 400 km needs 50 x 400/320 = 62.5 gallons.
rel: Fuel use is assumed proportional to distance.
